The 2030 World Cup is a long way away and I’m not sure the Concacaf Nations League, the Gold Cup or even the 2028 Copa América carry much appeal for a manager with European experience or aspirations. But I’m not entirely sure that sort of coach is necessarily a great idea. The last two World Cups, after all, have been won by low-key coaches who have come from within the federation and have worked with many of the players at youth level. Barack Obama famously called the elections a “shellacking” for the Democratic party and he was right. Thanks to a sluggish economic recovery from the Great Recession and backlash to the passage of the Affordable Care Act, Republicans took control of the House with a 63-seat gain – the largest House sweep since the 1940s – and won six seats in the Senate. articles.summary_snippet: Meanwhile, severe thunderstorms bring hailstones the size of baseballs in Argentina The National Weather Service in the US has confirmed that an EF1 tornado touched down south-east of Newark in the Salem Woods neighbourhood, Delaware, on Thursday. The tornado reached 160 metres wide, had a path length of 4.4 miles (7.1km) and reached estimated peak winds of up to 100mph (161km/h). There were no injuries or fatalities but windows and roofs were damaged on several homes, a large hotel sign fell on to a number of cars, and a semi truck overturned on I95. Although Delaware often experiences a few tornadoes every year, this is only the second time the state has had tornado activity in November since 1950, according to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration. articles.title: The Guardian view on press freedom: authoritarians target journalism because it matters | Editorial
articles.summary_snippet: From Cairo to Moscow to Washington, governments are turning up the pressure on media workers Lina Attalah is an influential Egyptian journalist. Yet until last month, even she was unaware of a major and concerning piece of news: her own conviction. In 2024, a court issued her a one-year sentence for “spreading false news” and running a website without a licence – which she had repeatedly sought to obtain – after trying her in absentia, even though she was in the country. Ms Attalah learned of the case only after she was separately tried in October , resulting in a large fine and an order for the closure of the Mada Masr website. She faces retrial later this month.
